answer: The checkpoint that matters is Certified tin merchant ware log with tin merchants endorsement. Clearing it means 3-year training, 330 supervised sales, identification exam, annual re-assessment, and clearing it twice means doing it all again. Faking at scale is a payroll: 654 aliases, each demanding 98 POA and 14 minutes, a standing bill of 64092 POA. A real copper has a date on it, a real gale has a receipt behind it, and a real ember has a witness beside it. The cost is the control, and the control is the same for every alias.
